subject: general
question: In a triangle PQR, RS intersects PQ at point S. The sides of the triangle QR = 36 cm, SQ = 27 cm, RS = 18 cm and ∠QRS = ∠QPR. What is the ratio of the perimeter of ∆PRS to that of ∆QSR?
solution:
Given:

In a ΔPQR, RS intersects PQ at point S.

QR = 36 cm

SQ = 27 cm

RS = 18 cm

∠QRS = ∠QPR

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2d3a1f6c3dc5d2ac7167745e60909afe64b364cc5d11757740c9ee04434fa125.png] 

In triangle PQR and QSR

∠QRS = ∠QPR (Given)

∠Q = ∠Q (Common)

So by AA rule, Δ PQR ∼ ΔQSR,

27/36 = 18/PR

PR = 24 cm

So, (27 + PS) / 36 = 36 / 27

PS = 48 - 27

PS = 21 cm

So, the ratio of the perimeter of ∆PRS to that of ∆QSR:

∆PRS / ∆QSR = (24 + 18 + 21) / (27 + 18 + 36) 

= 63 / 81

= (7)/(9)
